items.title: 66100_Bud Freeman oral history interview
items.q: was a fine guitarist, taught me chords

ctx.x: When I was -- I took a few lessons from Jimmy McPartland's father, who was a music teacher, and I didn't seem to like the lessons because that was -- I didn't like the discipline, you know, of sitting down and reading music at that time, and so I became bored with that and just went on my own way, which was sort of slow, but eventually I did learn how to improvise and did learn how to play the melody with the beat I had, and Dick McPartland,
Jimmy McPartland's brother, was a fine guitarist, taught me chords, and we just called them chords in those days. I didn't go very deeply into (unintelligible) studies until later.

And so that I could -- I knew what key I was playing in and I could -- when I improvised, I had an idea what the chord changes would be. Well, now at the age of 20, it appeared that I was going to have a serious music career. I wanted to be a jazz soloist because I was very involved and I was still listening endless hours to all of my jazz favorite records, of course, being Bix, Louis, Fats, James P., as I mentioned all the names, Ethel, and Bessie, and I found that I was learning more about jazz just through…
